new_statements.quote: The default prosodic pattern in SEM places lexical stress, which is realized by a raised tone melody, typically on the last syllable of the word. The raised tone melody is absent under two circumstances: in utterance-final syllables (where both downdrift and final prominence occur) and in final syllables of certain lexical pairs. [...] [conclusion, p. 29:] SEM has a default pitch rise on word boundaries. Since these tonal melodies are largely non-contrastive, these appear to be realizations of pitch accent or stress. Accent is placed on the last syllable of the word and is realized by a raised F0.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress (prosodic accent) falls by default on the final syllable of the word; it is realized mainly by raised pitch (a rising/high F0 melody) rather than intensity, and it is not contrastive except in a small set of otherwise homophonous pairs where one member carries penultimate prominence with a final falling pitch (incipient pitch-accent/tone).
new_statements.exceptions: (i) a handful of lexical pairs distinguished by prosody: bosi 'cloth' (final H) vs bosi 'louse' (penult + final falling), dasi 'we' vs dasi 'thread', chige 'ear' vs chige 'to see', wulang 'drinking' vs wulang 'many'; (ii) some inflectional suffixes (e.g. plural -si) do not attract stress, so prominence stays on the prior syllable; epenthetic vowels do not attract stress; (iii) utterance-final syllables show downdrift instead of the raised melody; (iv) Chinese loans take the same default final pattern regardless of original Chinese tone (unlike Baoan). Dwyer notes Slater 2003:103-104 treats both morphemes of some words as stressed.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (lexical stress/boundary tone), based on elicited words in isolation and carrier utterances with F0 measurements from one main speaker (Wang Xianzhen, Minhe) plus later field checks; utterance-level intonation explicitly set aside.
new_statements.identity_note: Dwyer 2008 calls the variety 'Southeastern Monguor (SEM)', defined as the Monguor of Minhe county (Qinghai), i.e. Minhe Mangghuer = minh1238; her ISO code MJG covers Monguor as a whole (Huzhu Mongghul huzh1238 is her 'Northern Monguor'). Data are chiefly from one Minhe speaker (Wang Xianzhen) checked against other speakers.

The raised tone melody is absent under two circumstances: in utterance-final syllables (where both downdrift and final prominence occur) and in final syllables of certain lexical pairs. sources.locator: preprint p. 7, sec. 2 'Contact environment and Mongolic prosody' (published pp. 111-128); confirmed in conclusion, preprint p. 29
sources.note: Default lexical stress, realized as a raised tone melody (raised F0), falls on the last syllable of the word; stress is not contrastive in Mongolic incl. SEM, but a small set of lexical pairs (bosi 'cloth' vs 'louse', dasi 'we' vs 'thread', chige 'ear' vs 'see', wulang 'drinking' vs 'many') now contrasts final H vs penult prominence + final falling pitch = incipient pitch-accent/tone; suffixes that do not attract stress leave prominence on the penult; Chinese loans get the same default final pattern regardless of source tone (sec. 2 p. 7, sec. 4 pp. 22-27, conclusion p. 29).

sources.note: Describes Huzhu Mongghul (huzh1238), not Mangghuer: sec. 4 'As a rule, the stress is on the final syllable of the word. Occasionally, the stress falls elsewhere'; explicitly treats Mangghuer as a different language. Not used for minh1238.
Nothing on stress, accent or tone; cites Slater 2003 for consonant allophony only.
